theories.claim: Every handleSprintQA* method in qa_handlers.go follows an identical contract: nil h.qa ⇒ ErrWebUnavailable via handleQueryError; non-nil call to the underlying QA method; on error propagate via handleQueryError with boolean=true (API surface); on success writeSuccess(http.StatusOK, result, nil).
theories.basis: Direct read of qa_handlers.go:10-166. Eleven handlers (handleSprintQA, handleSprintQAEvidence, handleSprintQAAdjudication, handleSprintQAIssues, handleSprintQAIssue, handleSprintQAAssessment, handleSprintQASmokeSuite, handleSprintQAMap, handleSprintQAShard, handleSprintQATheory, handleSprintQASynthesis) repeat the same shape; only handleSprintQAPage deviates by also calling h.queries.Sprint and rendering via h.render.
theories.confirmation_condition: Static reading shows uniform error/success handling across the eleven API handlers, with consistent booleans (true for API errors, false for page errors in handleSprintQAPage).
theories.refutation_condition: A handler deviates from the pattern (e.g., handles the error inline, returns a different status, or writes the body directly without handleQueryError/writeSuccess).
theories.inconclusive_condition: The semantics of handleQueryError's third boolean parameter and writeSuccess's collection argument cannot be fully resolved without reading handlers.go (outside the assigned paths).
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: Pure source reading of qa_handlers.go; no execution. Existing qa_handlers_test.go:38-57 partially exercises handleQueryError's stable-code mapping.

theories.claim: The Evidence/Adjudication/Issues/Issue/Assessment/SmokeSuite handlers skip the h.qa == nil guard and rely solely on a type assertion to app.QAEvidenceQueries, whereas handleSprintQA and related older handlers check nil before calling. If a future wiring ever injects a typed-nil QA service implementing QAEvidenceQueries, the type assertion succeeds and method calls would dispatch on a nil receiver.
theories.basis: qa_handlers.go:24 vs qa_handlers.go:11. The newer six handlers do 'queries, ok := h.qa.(app.QAEvidenceQueries)' without first checking h.qa == nil; the older five API handlers check nil then call h.qa.<Method> directly.
theories.confirmation_condition: Default wiring (h.qa nil interface ⇒ type assertion fails ⇒ ErrWebUnavailable) and unit-test coverage exist; qaQueryFixture in qa_handlers_test.go embeds *fakeQueries so QAEvidenceQueries assertion fails to find the methods unless the fixture provides them — confirming the failure path returns ErrWebUnavailable.
theories.refutation_condition: A wiring scenario sets h.qa to a typed-nil concrete type that implements QAEvidenceQueries; calls into QAEvidence/QAAdjudication/etc. would NPE inside the app layer.
theories.inconclusive_condition: Type-assertion safety under typed-nil is a real Go footgun; whether NewHandler/HandlerOptions rejects typed-nil injections is not visible in the assigned paths.
theories.safe_evidence_strategy: Static reading only; the qaQueryFixture in qa_handlers_test.go:17-33 shows the QAEvidenceQueries interface has at least six methods and the fixture implements them, so the type-assertion success path is exercised.
